chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from Abi Basir from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) would administer the beating (for drinking intoxicants) in the case of wine and nabidh: eighty for the free man, and the slave, and the Jew, and the Christian. I said: 'What is the matter with the Jew and the Christian?' He said: 'They do not have permission to make their drinking public; it happens in their houses.'
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for drinking wine in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani establishes the hadd of eighty lashes for consuming intoxicants, applying the penalty to both free individuals and slaves, as well as Jews and Christians. The scholar explains that the distinction for Ahl al-Kitab lies in the public nature of the punishment; since they typically consume alcohol privately within their homes, their drinking is not considered a public display of vice requiring public flogging.
